messages:
Support Ops: FYI escalation from AcmeRetail (T-4321). They see streaming sessions drop ~8-12s in hosted us-east for model gpt-retro-3b. Client sees 'Broken pipe'. Customer says many of these were billed as 5xx. Can we triage?

Maya Singh: assigning. Do we have request IDs or example request bodies?

Support Ops: Provided sample curl and one request id: req_0a7f3c. Says it was a long streaming response (>300 tokens) and client disconnected mid-stream. They included this repro: 

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  --no-buffer \
  --data-binary $'5\r\nhello\r\n0\r\n\r\n' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams
```

Support Ops: They also said aborting the client (ctrl-c) often led to a 502 in our logs and billing counted it as a 5xx.

James Park: grabbing logs for req_0a7f3c. Gateway shows: 
```
[2026-02-12T12:14:05Z] req=req_0a7f3c path=/v1/streams upstream=runtime-1 status=502 err=\"write /dev/fd/20: broken pipe\" conn=12345
[2026-02-12T12:14:05Z] req=req_0a7f3c gateway_code=499 client_abort=true
```
So upstream errored with EPIPE but gateway reported 502 to billing. There's a discrepancy in classification.

Maya Singh: looks like two separate things: a) chunked parser/state machine mishandling when client closes during middle of chunk b) metrics/classification pipeline mapping some client aborts -> 5xx in billing.

Eli Chen: I can repro locally. If the client sends a partial chunk (missing the final CRLF) and then closes, the runtime returns EPIPE when attempting to write remaining tokens. Our routing layer currently maps EPIPE -> upstream failure (502) instead of client closed (499). Easy repro: 
```
echo -ne "5\r\nhello" | nc api.redwood.example 443
# kill connection from client side before sending final CRLF
```

Lina Gomez: important: customer is billing-sensitive. If client disconnects are being billed as 5xx, we need to correct classification and backfill. Proposed immediate steps:
- treat EPIPE/EINVAL on write as client_abort and return 499 to metrics and billing
- add a new metric tag "client_disconnect=true" for all 499s from streaming paths
- patch chunked parser to tolerate truncated chunks and mark connection as client-abort earlier (less internal errors)

James Park: I ran a quick grep across past 7d: streaming paths had ~1.2k 502 spikes during customer window, of which ~760 show client_abort=true in raw gateway logs. Billing pipeline filters only look at http_status in aggregated view, which was 502. So we need to change pipeline to prefer gateway_code if present.

Support Ops: ACTION-1: open incident INC-2026-78 and notify billing + legal for potential refund.

Eli Chen: I'll push a small change to the gateway classifier: prefer gateway_code (499) over http_status when gateway detects client_abort flag. Add unit test for chunked-edge cases. Plan to canary in staging then prod. Estimated PR + canary: ~3h.

Maya Singh: can you also drop a quick repro script we can give to customer so they can validate client-side behavior?

Eli Chen: Sure. Minimal repro (force abort after sending partial chunk):
```
python - <<PY
import socket, time
s = socket.create_connection(("api.redwood.example", 443))
# perform TLS+http handshake omitted for brevity; use openssl s_client in practice
s.send(b"POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.example\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nAuthorization: Bearer <token>\r\n\r\n")
s.send(b"5\r\nhello")
# close early
s.close()
PY
```
This reliably produces EPIPE in the runtime and a gateway_code=499 entry in staging.

Lina Gomez: Billing asks: how many billed units to refund if we backfill? James, can you provide counts by customer?

James Park: yes. Running query now. For AcmeRetail we have ~43 sessions flagged as 502 during window; 37 of them have client_abort=true in trace logs. I'll export req ids and timestamps.

Support Ops: ACTION-2: Support to send exported req ids + timestamps to billing and cc eng-sre.

sre-bot: deploy/gateway-classifier-hotfix started by Eli Chen (canary=eng-staging). :rocket:

Eli Chen: canary looks good after 15m. Gateway now reports gateway_code=499 and we see no internal 502s being generated for these aborts. Pushing to prod in 30m.

sre-bot: deploy/gateway-classifier-hotfix succeeded in prod (id=deploy-2026-02-12-487). :white_check_mark:

James Park: I've also updated the metrics pipeline to prefer gateway_code when present and added tag client_disconnect. Historical backfill run started; ETA 4h.

Support Ops: Billing notified and acked receipt. They will run refund logic after backfill completes.

Maya Singh: follow-ups:
- ENG: postmortem for chunked parser + classifier (owner: Eli) - due in 72h
- SRE: confirm no customer-facing latency regressions after change (owner: James) - 24h observation
- Support: inform AcmeRetail of plan and provisional refund ETA (owner: Support Ops) - today

Lina Gomez: tagging this thread for visibility: @billing @legal @customer-success :eyes:

Support Ops: closing loop—customer updated with repro steps and we offered provisional refund. Will update thread when backfill completes.

Maya Singh: thanks team. Will convert this to a short postmortem once root cause is finalized.
